text: The seven Glyphs SDK plugin base classes over a plugin host (R025). They follow GlyphsSDK ObjectWrapper/GlyphsApp/plugins.py : the same defaults in init / loadPlugin , then the optional script hooks settings() and start() ; titles from menuName / name ; filters call filter(layer, inEditView, customParameters) ; reporters call foreground / background / inactiveLayerForeground / inactiveLayerBackground with getScale() set from the paint context. Where the SDK relies on Glyphs' native superclasses, the host does the work: FilterWithDialog.process_ restores each layer from its host snapshot before filtering (Glyphs copies shadowLayers ), and loadNib decodes the bundle's NIB/XIB into Qt-backed Cocoa views with this plugin as File's Owner. Exceptions in protocol methods go to the environment's error sink, as the SDK sends them to LogError . make_plugins_module(env) returns the GlyphsApp.plugins module with classes bound to env .

text: The plugin host contract on FontLab 9 (R025-R027). Menus: Glyphs menu names map to FontLab's main-window menus by title (FILE "File", EDIT "Edit", VIEW "View", GLYPH "Glyph", PATH "Contour", WINDOW "Window", SCRIPT "Script", HELP "Help"); FILTER_MENU and APP_MENU have no FontLab counterpart and go to an owned "Glyphs Plugins" menu. Each NSMenuItem becomes an owned QAction; its triggered runs item.fire() through the error sink, and item changes (title, state, enabled) update it. Panels and filter dialogs are owned tool windows (FontLab's own panel registry is not scriptable here); a dialog closes with Apply or Cancel. Painters go to :class: ~fontlab_glyport.drawing.editor.EditorPainters . Tools: FontLab exposes no Python tool registration (the flBasicTool wrapper only forwards activate/deactivate of native tools), so register_tool raises UnsupportedCapability (R054 candidate). File formats: a File-menu action "Export with <title>…" calls exportFont_ with the current font. Layers, fonts, snapshots and undo come from an injected model adapter (the GlyphsApp model of lane L1); without one those calls raise. Every token removes its widgets and connections exactly once; close() removes everything (newest first), attempting each and re-raising the first failure. Nothing is disconnected or deleted while a signal of the host's own widgets is dispatching (the PythonQtSignalReceiver crash pattern in AGENTS.md): dialog teardown, and any remove / close called from inside a host slot (a menu action, Apply/Cancel, a title-bar close, an on_close callback), run later from a process-wide single-shot "reaper" timer. That timer and its one connection live for the process, so it is never itself torn down inside its own dispatch.

text: Load a plugin class into a host and unload it deterministically (R025-R027). load_plugin(cls, env) creates the instance the SDK way ( alloc().init() then loadPlugin() ) and registers what its protocol needs: FilterWithoutDialog: a FILTER_MENU item running filter(layer, True, {}) on the selected layers inside one undo group. FilterWithDialog: a FILTER_MENU item that snapshots the selected layers, opens the plugin's view in a host dialog ( setup() previews), keeps the result on Apply and restores the snapshots on Cancel, in one undo group. PalettePlugin: a host panel with theView() . ReporterPlugin: a VIEW_MENU toggle "Show <title>"; while on, painters for each hook the plugin defines (foreground/background, active/inactive). If the host refuses before-native drawing (FontLab R054), background hooks paint in the post-native overlay. REPORTER_BACKGROUND_AS_OVERLAY records "background drawn as overlay" in the execution receipt: ink is above the native outlines, rather than below them. SelectTool: register_tool . FileFormatPlugin: register_file_format . GeneralPlugin: nothing; its start() adds menus through Glyphs.menu . A register_* call the host cannot honour ( UnsupportedCapability ) becomes a diagnostic; the rest of the plugin stays loaded. A failure in init / loadPlugin gives a failed handle with everything registered so far removed (R027). unload() removes tokens newest first, once.

text: Read compiled NIBs (no Objective-C runtime) into plain Python objects (R031). Two container formats occur in Glyphs plugin bundles: NIBArchive (the default since macOS 10.13; a single file or keyedobjects-101300.nib ) and NSKeyedArchiver binary plists ( keyedobjects.nib ). Both decode to the same shape: :class: Archived objects (class name plus fields) with strings, numbers and collections already turned into Python values. A .nib directory is read through its keyed archive when present. NIBArchive layout, all integers little-endian: magic, two format words, then (count, offset) pairs for objects, keys, values and class names. Variable integers keep 7 bits per byte, and a set high bit marks the last byte. Value types: 0-3 signed ints of 1/2/4/8 bytes, 4 false, 5 true, 6 float, 7 double, 8 data (length-prefixed), 9 nil, 10 object reference (4 bytes). Collections store their elements under the repeated key UINibEncoderEmptyKey . Hostile input is rejected with :class: NibFormatError , never expanded: files over MAX_BYTES , variable integers wider than 5 bytes (32 bits), table counts larger than the file, offsets and references outside their tables, reference chains deeper than MAX_DECODE_DEPTH , and any malformed record. Shared and cyclic references decode once (memoised by object index).

text: XIB sources and compiled NIBs as one UIGraph (R028, R031). Both readers emit the same node schema, so a NIB with no XIB source and the XIB it came from produce equal graphs (the tests compare them): source_class is the AppKit class ( NSTextField ); a custom class is in properties["customClass"] ( GSSteppingTextField , GSPaletteView ). Placeholders are NSCustomObject nodes with properties["role"] : owner (File's Owner, with className ), firstResponder or application ; other custom objects have role object . Views carry frame [x, y, w, h] in Cocoa's bottom-left coordinates, autoresizingMask (Interface Builder's default 12, top-left pinned) and hidden . Controls add the keys their class uses: title , editable , bezeled , buttonType , state , minValue , maxValue , value , items , selectedIndex , continuous , enabled , toolTip . Connections: outlet (owner node -> destination, selector = property; an outlet to a control's cell points at the control), action (control -> target, selector = action), binding (control -> controller, selector = binding name, argument = key path), constraint (first item -> second item, or the first item again for a constant; selector "<attribute> <relation> <attribute>" , argument "<multiplier> <constant> <priority>" ). A tab view's items are its child NSView pages with tabLabel and tabIdentifier ; text fields with a number formatter carry formatter {"minimum", "maximum"} , and a standalone formatter is an NSNumberFormatter node with the limits it sets; progress indicators carry minValue , maxValue , value and indeterminate . A matrix carries rows , columns , mode , cellSize , intercellSpacing and cells : row-major button cells, each with title , buttonType , state , tag and enabled . A box carries boxType , titlePosition , borderType , transparent and title ( "" when no title is shown); its only child is its content view, marked contentView . A scroll view carries hasVerticalScroller , hasHorizontalScroller , autohidesScrollers and a custom clipViewClass ; its only child is its clip view's document view, marked documentView (the clip view and scrollers are not nodes). An array controller is an NSArrayController node; each table column is also an NSTableColumn child node ( index ) so bindings can name it. A table view carries columns ( identifier , title , width , minWidth , maxWidth , editable ), headerVisible , allowsMultipleSelection , rowHeight and prototypes : for a view-based table, each prototype cell view as its own graph JSON keyed by identifier (File's Owner = the makeViewWithIdentifier_owner_ owner). Buttons also carry bordered and, with a named image, image and imagePosition ; a switch carries state . A text view carries string (plain text), editable and selectable . A split view carries vertical and dividerStyle (its subviews are the panes); a grid view carries rows , columns , rowSpacing and columnSpacing (its cells' content views are its children); a visual effect view is a plain container. A segmented control carries segments ( label , width , selected , tag , image ) and trackingMode ; a search field adds placeholder and sendsSearchStringImmediately to the text field properties. A combo box carries title (its text), editable , items , completes , numberOfVisibleItems and usesDataSource . A path control carries url (a URL string), editable and allowedTypes . An image view carries image (a resource name) and imageScaling . A stack view carries orientation (0 horizontal, 1 vertical), alignment (an NSLayoutAttribute), distribution , spacing , edgeInsets [top, left, bottom, right] and detachesHiddenViews ; its children (the arranged views) carry arranged . A window ( NSWindow or NSPanel ; a custom subclass in customClass ) carries title , styleMask and contentRect (screen coordinates, bottom-left); its content view is its only child, marked contentView . Nodes keep document order (XIB) or archive order of NSSubviews (NIB). Elements the readers do not translate still become nodes (class xib:<element> or the archived class); the loader decides what is blocked.

text: Call PythonQt methods that return lists of QObject pointers safely. Native fact (FontLab 9.0.9780, PythonQt; evidence glyport-ui/native-fix-round1-* and l2-markers.log.fault in the L2 report): QApplication.topLevelWidgets() segfaulted in PythonQtPrivate::wrapPtr while converting the list. Wrapping each pointer allocates Python objects, which can trigger the cyclic garbage collector; if that collects a Python-owned widget in the list, PythonQt deletes it and the next pointer in the list is dangling. qt_list keeps the collector off for the duration of the call and the conversion (reference counting still runs). GUI thread only (enforced): Qt widgets live there, and gc.disable() is process-wide, so a call from another thread could re-enable collection while the GUI thread is still converting. It does not stop an explicit gc.collect() or reference-count destruction.
